# Coach debrief — 2026-09-28

> Debriefed with Claude directly (the app's coach server is not reachable from the deployed site yet).

## you

Finished a 15-minute short class. Rides a bicycle to work and back every day, so some
areas are very tight. Low ceilings at home make standing postures with the arms
stretched overhead difficult. Has tonsil stones and is trying to get rid of them. A
teacher, on his feet walking around all day.

## coach (Claude)

Reading: daily cycling shortens the hip flexors and quads, tightens the hamstrings and
calves, and rounds the upper back and shoulders over the bars; a day of walking loads the
calves, feet and low back on top. Low ceilings rule out the overhead reaches while
standing (Half Moon, Balancing Stick, Standing Separate Leg Head to Knee, the arm-up half
of Standing Bow). Tonsil stones are not something a posture removes — that is hydration,
gargling and, if they persist, a doctor — but the throat-opening postures (Camel, and the
neck line of Rabbit later) are traditionally said to help the throat, and they cost
nothing. Knees: Fixed Firm is the best thing in the sequence for a cyclist's quads and
ankles, but only as deep as the knees allow — elbows, not shoulders, if they lift.

Proposed next class, first sets, ≈23 minutes:
